text:
marco: Heads-up — we saw a big p95 DNS resolve spike (~400-800ms) for internal service calls right after the large GPU batch deploy in us-east-1. App errors and retries spiked. Anyone else seeing this?

tara: I saw the alerts. Correlates with the reserved-gpu ASG scale-up + ~120 new pods starting over 3m. node-local-dns miss rate jumped. Logs show a TON of UDP retries.

anya: Dumped CoreDNS metrics: `coredns_request_duration_seconds{quantile=0.95}` jumped to ~0.48. node-local-cache miss ratio went from 0.02 -> 0.37.

michael: Also seeing TCP fallback for some lookups (we prefer UDP). Could be fragmentation/MTU: lots of `ICMP frag needed` in the node dmesg around the same time.

kyle: RDMA NIC errors? I pulled logs from a couple of the gpu nodes and found intermittent `mlx5_core` WARNs around pod start churn. Might be packet loss on the east-west path causing UDP retransmits and truncation.

marco: timeline: 12:10 deploy-bot kicked off batch, 12:11 ASG scaled 20 instances, 12:12 kubelet churn started, 12:13 DNS p95 spike.

sre-bot: incident: dns-resolve-p95-spike created. Severity: P2.

tara: Quick repro: scale down a small set, then scale back up; within ~30-90s the pod creation fanout causes many simultaneous service lookups (readiness probes + registries) hitting node-local-dns and CoreDNS. The node-local cache evictions line up with that.

anya: Commands I ran:
```
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=node-local-dns -o wide
kubectl logs -n kube-system node-local-dns-abcde -c node-local-dns
curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=coredns_request_duration_seconds%7Bquantile%3D%220.95%22%7D
```

michael: Network datapoints: iperf between two gpu nodes showed ~1% packet loss during the window; tcpdump on node-local-dns showed repeated truncated UDP fragments for ~150ms bursts. MTU mismatch? We did a customer-requested overlay update last week.

kyle: Confirmed MTU on the new instances was 1500 but upstream fabric expects jumbo 9000. Usually the CNI sets mtu but seems some instances didn't pick up the new config during bootstrap. Fragmentation + RDMA offload weirdness => retries.

marco: OK — possible root causes: (1) pod churn causing large concurrent DNS fanout, (2) node-local-dns cache thrash + eviction, (3) MTU mismatch leading to UDP fragmentation and retransmits, (4) transient RDMA errors exacerbating packet loss.

anya: Short-term mitigations I applied: restarted node-local-dns DaemonSet on a subset of nodes in the affected AZ (rolling) which reduced miss rate and p95 within ~2 minutes. Also bumped node-local-dns cache size temporarily.

michael: I pushed a kernel nic offload tweak to the canary group: disabled GRO for the affected NICs and that reduced packet reassembly hiccups in the short window. Not a long-term fix.

kyle: Suggested infra fixes: enforce MTU at provisioning (cloud-init) and add a post-provision check that validates `ip link` MTU and the CNI config before joining the cluster. Also add RDMA driver health probe to the node startup readiness.

tara: Product note — the deploy pattern that starts hundreds of pods quickly is common for GPU workloads (batch jobs). We should consider making the GPU scaling path less bursty: pre-warm nodes or stagger pod startup to reduce fanout.

marco: Action items:
- kyle: add MTU check to node bootstrap + ticket to backfill cloud-init images (ETA 2d)
- anya: add a one-off Prometheus alert for node-local-dns miss ratio and increase scrape resolution during scale events (ETA 4h)
- michael: run an RDMA health job against the next GPU node AMI build and add to image validation (ETA 1d)
- tara: put together a small doc for safer GPU scale patterns and a guideline to stagger readiness probes (ETA 1d)

anya: Also adding a short-runbook entry: if you see DNS p95 spike during large scale events — restart node-local-dns DaemonSet on a few nodes in the AZ (avoid all at once), validate node MTU, and check `dmesg` for mlx5/ib warnings.

marco: Will also coordinate with capacity planning to reduce concurrent scale aggressiveness overnight if we see repeat flakiness. Cost tradeoff: pre-warm increases reserved minutes but lowers error surface. We should model the cost vs error rate.

kyle: I'll open the infra PR for the MTU check now and link it here.

michael: I'll schedule an AMI test run with RDMA probe against the next canary batch.

marco: Thanks team. Please drop any logs or dashboards here. If anyone sees a repeat spike, @here call it out ASAP so we can trigger the runbook. :thumbsup:
